records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוָ֣ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֣ה בְמִדְבַּר־סִ֠ינַי בַּשָּׁנָ֨ה הַשֵּׁנִ֜ית לְצֵאתָ֨ם מֵאֶ֧רֶץ מִצְרַ֛יִם בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֖וֹן לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses in [the] wilderness of Sinai, in the year the second of their going out from [the] land of Egypt, in the month the first, saying,
pieces: In the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt, in its first month, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai and said,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the second year of their going out from the land of Egypt, in the first month, saying,

R.1: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses in the Sinai Desert. It was the first month of the second year after the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had left Egypt. He said,

decisions.choice: the first month of the second year: a month before the census of chapter 1
decisions.reason: The book opens on the first day of the second month (1:1), but this speech comes a month earlier. The tabernacle had been set up on the first day of the first month of the second year (Exodus 40:17), and the Passover fell on the fourteenth day of that month (verse 3). The story goes back in time here to tell how the first Passover after Egypt was kept, and how the cloud led the people from the day the tabernacle was set up (verse 15).

decisions.choice: their going out: Israel's leaving Egypt
decisions.reason: "Their" refers to the people of Israel, though they have not been named in the verse. Years are counted from the exodus, as in 1:1 and Exodus 19:1.

decisions.choice: the Israelites
decisions.reason: Readable names the people that "their" refers to, and splits the verse into short sentences.

records.heading: The Passover in the wilderness of Sinai

records.source: וְיַעֲשׂ֧וּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת־הַפָּ֖סַח בְּמוֹעֲדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And let observe [the] sons of Israel the Passover at its appointed time.
pieces: "The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} are to keep the Passover at its appointed time.

L.2: "And let the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel keep the Passover at its appointed time.

R.2: "The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} must celebrate the Passover at the set time.

decisions.choice: observe the Passover: prepare and hold the Passover meal
decisions.reason: The verb is the common word "do" or "make". With "Passover" it means to slaughter the lamb and hold the feast as the law lays it down (Exodus 12:47-48). The same phrase runs through verses 2-14.

decisions.choice: its appointed time: the fixed date of the feast
decisions.reason: The word names a set time or season fixed by God. Verse 3 gives the date, as Exodus 12:6 and Leviticus 23:5 do. This is the first Passover after the one kept in Egypt, a year after the people left.

decisions.choice: keep / celebrate
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "keep" the Passover, the usual word for holding a feast as required. Readable says "celebrate", a more familiar word.

records.source: בְּאַרְבָּעָ֣ה עָשָֽׂר־י֠וֹם בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֜ה בֵּ֧ין הָֽעֲרְבַּ֛יִםתַּעֲשׂ֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ בְּמוֹעֲד֑וֹ כְּכָל־חֻקֹּתָ֥יו וּכְכָל־מִשְׁפָּטָ֖יו תַּעֲשׂ֥וּ אֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: On [the] fourteenth day in this month, between the evenings, you will observe it at its appointed time; according to all its statutes and according to all its judgments you will observe it.
pieces: On the fourteenth day of this month, at dusk, you are to keep it at its appointed time, following all its statutes and rulings."

L.3: On the fourteenth day of this month, between the two evenings, you shall keep it at its appointed time; according to all its statutes and according to all its judgments you shall keep it."

R.3: Celebrate it in the evening of the fourteenth day of this month, at the set time. Follow all its laws and rules when you do."

decisions.choice: between the two evenings: at twilight, as the day ends
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 12:6. The phrase is used for the Passover and for the evening offering, and its exact meaning is uncertain: between sunset and dark, or between the afternoon and sunset. Deuteronomy 16:6 places the Passover sacrifice at sunset.

decisions.choice: all its statutes and all its judgments: every rule laid down for the feast
decisions.reason: The two words together cover the whole of what the law requires for the Passover: the lamb, the blood, the meal and the bread without yeast (Exodus 12:1-28, 43-49). Verses 11-12 repeat some of these rules.

decisions.choice: at dusk / in the evening
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the plain sense of the idiom; Literal keeps "between the two evenings".

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַעֲשֹׂ֥ת הַפָּֽסַח׃
records.gloss: And spoke Moses to [the] sons of Israel to observe the Passover.
pieces: So Moses told the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to keep the Passover.

L.4: And Moses spoke to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, to keep the Passover.

R.4: So Moses told the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to celebrate the Passover.

decisions.choice: So Moses told
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "so" for "and": Moses passes on to the people what the LORD said to him.

records.source: וַיַּעֲשׂ֣וּ אֶת־הַפֶּ֡סַח בָּרִאשׁ֡וֹן בְּאַרְבָּעָה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר י֥וֹם לַחֹ֛דֶשׁ בֵּ֥ין הָעַרְבַּ֖יִם בְּמִדְבַּ֣ר סִינָ֑י כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֔ה כֵּ֥ן עָשׂ֖וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And they observed the Passover in the first [month], on [the] fourteenth day of the month, between the evenings, in [the] wilderness of Sinai; according to all that had commanded Yahweh Moses, so did [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: They kept the Passover in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at dusk, in the wilderness of Sinai. Everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did.

L.5: And they kept the Passover in the first [month], on the fourteenth day of the month, between the two evenings, in the wilderness of Sinai; according to all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses, so the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did.

R.5: They celebrated the Passover in the Sinai Desert on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did everything that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

decisions.choice: in the first: in the first month
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "in the first"; "month" is understood from verse 1.

decisions.choice: according to all ... so they did: full obedience
decisions.reason: This is the way the books of Moses mark that the people did exactly what God commanded, as when the tabernacle was finished (Exodus 39:32, 42-43; 40:16) and when the census was made (Numbers 1:54). It sets up the question of verses 6-7: what of those who could not obey?

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י אֲנָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָי֤וּ טְמֵאִים֙ לְנֶ֣פֶשׁ אָדָ֔ם וְלֹא־יָכְל֥וּ לַעֲשֹׂת־הַפֶּ֖סַח בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַֽיִּקְרְב֞וּ לִפְנֵ֥י מֹשֶׁ֛ה וְלִפְנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹ֖ן בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And there were men who were unclean for [the] corpse of a person, and not they were able to observe the Passover on that day; and they drew near before Moses and before Aaron on that day.
pieces: But there were some men who were unclean from contact with a dead body, and so they could not keep the Passover on that day. That same day they came before Moses and Aaron.

L.6: And there were men who were unclean because of the dead body of a person, and they could not keep the Passover on that day; and they came near before Moses and before Aaron on that day.

R.6: But some men had touched a dead body, so they were unclean. Because of this they could not celebrate the Passover that day. That same day they went to Moses and Aaron.

decisions.choice: the nefesh of a person: a dead body
decisions.reason: The word *nefesh* usually means a living being or a life. In laws about uncleanness it can mean a dead person, a corpse (Leviticus 21:11; Numbers 6:6; 19:11, 13). "Of a person" makes clear it is a human body.

decisions.choice: unclean, so not able to keep the Passover
decisions.reason: Contact with a dead body made a person unclean for seven days (19:11-12). Someone unclean could not eat holy food such as the meat of offerings (Leviticus 7:20-21), so these men could not share the Passover lamb. Their uncleanness was no fault of theirs; someone has to bury the dead.

decisions.choice: on that day ... on that day: the same day as the Passover
decisions.reason: The phrase is repeated. They came to Moses and Aaron on the very day the feast was being kept, when they found they could not join in.

decisions.choice: from contact with / had touched
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "unclean for a dead body". Balanced and Readable say how the body made them unclean, as 19:11 states.

records.source: וַ֠יֹּאמְרוּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָהֵ֨מָּה֙ אֵלָ֔יו אֲנַ֥חְנוּ טְמֵאִ֖ים לְנֶ֣פֶשׁ אָדָ֑ם לָ֣מָּה נִגָּרַ֗ע לְבִלְתִּ֨י הַקְרִ֜ב אֶת־קָרְבַּ֤ן יְהוָה֙ בְּמֹ֣עֲד֔וֹ בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And said the men those to him, we [are] unclean for [the] corpse of a person; why should we be held back so as not to bring near the offering of Yahweh at its appointed time among [the] sons of Israel?
pieces: Those men said to him, "We are unclean because of a dead body. Must we be shut out, then, and not bring the offering of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at its appointed time with the rest of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}?"

L.7: And those men said to him, "We [are] unclean because of the dead body of a person. Why should we be held back from bringing near the offering of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at its appointed time among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel?"

R.7: They said to Moses, "We are unclean because we touched a dead body. But why should we be left out? Why can we not bring the offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the set time, along with the other {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}?"

decisions.choice: to him: to Moses
decisions.reason: Verse 6 names Moses and Aaron, but "him" is singular, and Moses answers in verse 8. Moses is the one who brings the question to the LORD.

decisions.choice: held back: made to lose what belongs to them
decisions.reason: The verb means to be reduced or to have something taken away (27:4; 36:3-4). The men ask not to lose their share in the feast that belongs to every Israelite.

decisions.choice: the offering of Yahweh: the Passover lamb
decisions.reason: The Passover lamb is here called an offering "brought near" to the LORD, the language used of sacrifices (Leviticus 1:2). Verse 13 uses the same words.

decisions.choice: Must we be shut out / why should we be left out
decisions.reason: The men's question is a protest, not a request for information. Balanced and Readable put it as the complaint it is; Readable splits it into two questions.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֖ם מֹשֶׁ֑ה עִמְד֣וּ וְאֶשְׁמְעָ֔ה מַה־יְצַוֶּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לָכֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And said to them Moses, stand, and let me hear what will command Yahweh concerning you.
pieces: Moses said to them, "Stay here, and let me hear what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will command for you."

L.8: And Moses said to them, "Stand, and let me hear what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will command concerning you."

R.8: Moses said, "Wait here. I will find out what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says you should do."

decisions.choice: stand: wait, stay where you are
decisions.reason: The verb means to stand still or remain. Moses asks the men to wait while he seeks the LORD's answer.

decisions.choice: let me hear what Yahweh will command: Moses does not decide alone
decisions.reason: Where the law has given no ruling, Moses takes the case to the LORD and waits for his word, as in Leviticus 24:12 and Numbers 15:34; 27:5. Verses 9-14 give the answer.

decisions.choice: I will find out
decisions.reason: Readable says "find out" for "let me hear": Moses will listen for the LORD's answer.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,

L.9: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: the LORD answers the men's question
decisions.reason: The answer goes further than the men's case: it gives a rule for the future that covers both the unclean and the traveler (verse 10).

records.heading: A Passover in the second month

records.source: דַּבֵּ֛ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר אִ֣ישׁ אִ֣ישׁ כִּי־יִהְיֶֽה־טָמֵ֣א׀לָנֶ֡פֶשׁ אוֹ֩ בְדֶ֨רֶךְ רְחֹקָ֜הׄלָכֶ֗ם א֚וֹ לְדֹרֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וְעָ֥שָׂה פֶ֖סַח לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel, saying, a man, a man, when he is unclean for a corpse, or on a journey distant, of you or of your generations, and he will observe a Passover to Yahweh.
pieces: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'Any of you, now or in generations to come, who is unclean because of a dead body or is away on a distant journey may still keep a Passover for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.10: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, saying, 'If {{gender:anyone|any man}} of you or of your generations is unclean because of a dead body, or [is] on a distant journey, he shall keep a Passover to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.10: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'Someone among you or your descendants may be unclean from touching a dead body, or may be far away on a trip. That person may still celebrate the Passover for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a man, a man: anyone at all
decisions.reason: Saying the word twice means "each one, whoever it is" (Leviticus 17:3; Numbers 5:12). The rule covers every Israelite, man or woman.

decisions.choice: distant: a scribal dot stands over one letter
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew manuscripts a dot is written above a letter of the word for "distant", one of a few places in the books of Moses with such dots. The dot does not change the words that are read, and its purpose is uncertain; it may mark a doubt the scribes had about the word. Jewish tradition took it to mean that "distant" should not be pressed: anyone away from the place of the feast at the time counts (Mishnah Pesahim 9:2).

decisions.choice: of you or of your generations: a rule for all time
decisions.reason: The ruling is not only for these men. It holds for later generations too, like the Passover itself (Exodus 12:14).

decisions.choice: he shall keep a Passover: permission, and also a duty
decisions.reason: The verb form is the one used for laws ("he shall keep"). It grants what the men asked for, a way to take part, and it also makes clear that the Passover is not to be skipped but kept a month later (verse 11).

decisions.choice: may still keep
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "still" and say "may", since the rule answers the men's request in verse 7. Literal keeps "he shall keep". Balanced and Readable avoid "he" for a rule that covers everyone.

records.source: בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֜י בְּאַרְבָּעָ֨ה עָשָׂ֥ר י֛וֹם בֵּ֥ין הָעַרְבַּ֖יִם יַעֲשׂ֣וּ אֹת֑וֹ עַל־מַצּ֥וֹת וּמְרֹרִ֖ים יֹאכְלֻֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: In the month the second, on [the] fourteenth day, between the evenings, they will observe it; with unleavened bread and bitter herbs they will eat it.
pieces: In the second month, at dusk on the fourteenth day, they are to keep it, eating it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

L.11: In the second month, on the fourteenth day, between the two evenings, they shall keep it; with unleavened bread and bitter herbs they shall eat it.

R.11: They must celebrate it in the evening of the fourteenth day of the second month. They must eat the lamb with bread made without yeast and with bitter herbs.

decisions.choice: the second month: one month after the set date
decisions.reason: The date is the same as in verse 3, a month later. In the time of King Hezekiah the whole people kept the Passover in the second month, because the priests and people had not made themselves clean in time (2 Chronicles 30:2-3, 15).

decisions.choice: unleavened bread and bitter herbs: the Passover meal
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 12:8. The bread made without yeast recalled the haste of leaving Egypt (Exodus 12:39); the bitter herbs are not explained there, but they have been taken as a reminder of the bitterness of slavery (Exodus 1:14 uses a related word).

decisions.choice: the lamb
decisions.reason: "It" is the Passover lamb, which Readable names. Readable also says "bread made without yeast" for "unleavened bread", as in Exodus 12:8.

records.source: לֹֽא־יַשְׁאִ֤ירוּ מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ עַד־בֹּ֔קֶר וְעֶ֖צֶם לֹ֣א יִשְׁבְּרוּ־ב֑וֹ כְּכָל־חֻקַּ֥ת הַפֶּ֖סַח יַעֲשׂ֥וּ אֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Not they will leave over of it until morning, and a bone not they will break in it; according to every statute of the Passover they will observe it.
pieces: None of it is to be left over until morning, and no bone of it is to be broken. They are to keep it by every statute of the Passover.

L.12: They shall not leave any of it until morning, and a bone they shall not break in it; according to every statute of the Passover they shall keep it.

R.12: They must not leave any of it until the next morning, and they must not break any of its bones. They must follow all the rules for the Passover.

decisions.choice: a bone you shall not break: the rules of Exodus 12 apply in full
decisions.reason: The two rules come from Exodus 12:10 and 12:46. John 19:36 quotes the words about the bone of Jesus on the cross, whose legs were not broken.

decisions.choice: according to every statute: the same feast, not a lesser one
decisions.reason: The Passover kept a month late is to be kept in full, by every rule of the first. It is the same Passover held at a different time.

decisions.choice: None of it is to be left over ... no bone of it is to be broken
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the two commands into passive statements, as Exodus 12:46 does in Readable; the rules apply to everyone at the meal.

records.source: וְהָאִישׁ֩ אֲשֶׁר־ה֨וּא טָה֜וֹר וּבְדֶ֣רֶךְ לֹא־הָיָ֗ה וְחָדַל֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת הַפֶּ֔סַח וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מֵֽעַמֶּ֑יהָ כִּ֣י׀קָרְבַּ֣ן יְהוָ֗ה לֹ֤א הִקְרִיב֙ בְּמֹ֣עֲד֔וֹ חֶטְא֥וֹ יִשָּׂ֖א הָאִ֥ישׁ הַהֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And the man who [is] clean and on a journey not was, and refrains from observing the Passover, and will be cut off the person that from its kin; for [the] offering of Yahweh not he brought near at its appointed time; his sin will bear the man that.
pieces: But anyone who is clean and is not on a journey, and yet holds back from keeping the Passover, is to be cut off from their people. They did not present the offering of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at its appointed time, and they will bear the guilt of their sin.

L.13: But {{gender:the person|the man}} who [is] clean and was not on a journey, and fails to keep the Passover, that person shall be cut off from his people, for he did not bring near the offering of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at its appointed time; that {{gender:person|man}} shall bear his sin.

R.13: But suppose someone is clean and is not away on a trip, and still does not celebrate the Passover. That person must be cut off from their people, because they did not bring the offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the set time. They must suffer the punishment for their sin.

decisions.choice: fails: holds back, chooses not to
decisions.reason: The verb means to stop or refrain from doing something. The person has no reason to miss the feast and simply does not keep it, unlike the men of verse 6.

decisions.choice: cut off from his people: removed from the people of God
decisions.reason: The law uses this phrase for serious offenses against the covenant (Genesis 17:14; Exodus 12:15, 19). It does not say how the cutting off happens; in some laws God himself does it (Leviticus 20:3-6), and it may mean death or the end of a family line. Passover marked who belonged to Israel, so refusing it was refusing to belong.

decisions.choice: bear his sin: carry the guilt and its penalty
decisions.reason: To "bear sin" is to be held guilty and to face its consequences (Leviticus 5:1; 24:15; Numbers 18:22).

decisions.choice: the man ... that person: anyone, man or woman
decisions.reason: The law speaks of "the man" and "the person" in turn. It applies to every Israelite who refuses the Passover.

decisions.choice: anyone ... their
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use inclusive words for a law about anyone, since the Hebrew "man" and "person" here stand for everyone. Literal uses the gender setting for "the man".

records.source: וְכִֽי־יָג֨וּר אִתְּכֶ֜ם גֵּ֗ר וְעָ֤שָֽׂה פֶ֨סַח֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה כְּחֻקַּ֥ת הַפֶּ֛סַח וּכְמִשְׁפָּט֖וֹ כֵּ֣ן יַעֲשֶׂ֑ה חֻקָּ֤ה אַחַת֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֔ם וְלַגֵּ֖ר וּלְאֶזְרַ֥ח הָאָֽרֶץ׃פ
records.gloss: And when sojourns with you a sojourner and he would observe a Passover to Yahweh, according to [the] statute of the Passover and according to its judgment, so he will do; one statute will be for you, both for the sojourner and for [the] native of the land.
pieces: If a foreigner living among you wants to keep a Passover for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, it must be kept by the statute and the ruling for the Passover. There is to be one statute for you all, for the foreigner and for the one born in the land.'"

L.14: And when a sojourner sojourns with you and would keep a Passover to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, according to the statute of the Passover and according to its judgment, so he shall do; one statute shall be for you, both for the sojourner and for the native of the land.'"

R.14: Foreigners who live among you may also celebrate the Passover for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. But they must follow all its laws and rules. The same law is for everyone, both foreigners and people born Israelites.'"

decisions.choice: a sojourner who sojourns with you: a foreigner settled among Israel
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 12:48: someone living away from his own people, without the rights of those born in the land.

decisions.choice: and would keep a Passover: if he wishes to
decisions.reason: The foreigner is not required to keep the Passover, but he may. Exodus 12:48 adds the condition: every male of his household must first be circumcised.

decisions.choice: one statute for the sojourner and the native: the same terms for both
decisions.reason: The rule of Exodus 12:49 is repeated: a foreigner who joins in keeps the feast by the same law as an Israelite by birth (Leviticus 24:22; Numbers 15:15-16).

decisions.choice: foreigner living among you
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 12:48; Literal keeps "sojourner".

decisions.choice: people born Israelites
decisions.reason: "The native of the land" is an Israelite by birth, as in Exodus 12:19; Readable says so.

records.source: וּבְיוֹם֙ הָקִ֣ים אֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן כִּסָּ֤ה הֶֽעָנָן֙ אֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן לְאֹ֖הֶל הָעֵדֻ֑ת וּבָעֶ֜רֶב יִהְיֶ֧ה עַֽל־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן כְּמַרְאֵה־אֵ֖שׁ עַד־בֹּֽקֶר׃
records.gloss: And on [the] day of setting up the tabernacle, covered the cloud the tabernacle, of the tent of the testimony; and in the evening it was over the tabernacle like [the] appearance of fire until morning.
pieces: The day the tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered the tabernacle, the tent of the testimony, and from evening until morning it hung over the tabernacle with the look of fire.

L.15: And on the day of setting up the tabernacle, the cloud covered the tabernacle, the tent of the testimony; and in the evening it would be over the tabernacle like an appearance of fire until morning.

R.15: On the day the tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered it. This was the tent where the covenant tablets were kept. In the evening the cloud over the tabernacle looked like fire, and it stayed that way until morning.

decisions.choice: the day of setting up the tabernacle: the day told in Exodus 40
decisions.reason: The tabernacle was set up on the first day of the first month of the second year, and the cloud covered it and the glory of the LORD filled it (Exodus 40:17, 34-38). Verses 15-23 go back to that day and describe how the cloud led Israel from then on, before the first move from Sinai in 10:11-12.

decisions.choice: the tabernacle, of the tent of the testimony: the tabernacle, that is, the tent
decisions.reason: A small word links the two names. It most likely just says which tabernacle is meant: the tent of the testimony. It may instead name the part the cloud covered, the tent over the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: the testimony: the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: "The testimony" is the two stone tablets of the covenant, kept in the ark inside the tent (Exodus 25:16, 21; 31:18). The tent is named after them.

decisions.choice: it would be: what happened every night
decisions.reason: The verb describes a repeated pattern: night after night the cloud over the tabernacle looked like fire.

decisions.choice: the tent where the covenant tablets were kept
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the tent of the testimony" in its own sentence; Literal and Balanced keep the name.

records.heading: The cloud over the tabernacle

records.source: כֵּ֚ן יִהְיֶ֣ה תָמִ֔יד הֶעָנָ֖ן יְכַסֶּ֑נּוּ וּמַרְאֵה־אֵ֖שׁ לָֽיְלָה׃
records.gloss: So it was continually: the cloud covered it, and [the] appearance of fire [by] night.
pieces: This went on all the time: the cloud covered it, and by night there was what looked like fire.

L.16: So it was continually: the cloud would cover it, and the appearance of fire by night.

R.16: This happened all the time. The cloud covered the tabernacle, and at night it looked like fire.

decisions.choice: the cloud covered it: the Hebrew has no "by day"
alternatives: the cloud covered it by day
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek, Syriac and Latin translations read "the cloud covered it by day", balancing "by night" at the end. The Hebrew text lacks "by day", but the sense is the same: cloud by day, fire by night (Exodus 13:21-22; 40:38).

decisions.choice: continually: every day and night of the journey
decisions.reason: The verse sums up verse 15: what happened on the first day went on from then on.

decisions.choice: the tabernacle
decisions.reason: Readable names what "it" refers to.

records.source: וּלְפִ֞י הֵעָלֹ֤ת הֶֽעָנָן֙ מֵעַ֣ל הָאֹ֔הֶל וְאַ֣חֲרֵי־כֵ֔ן יִסְע֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּבִמְק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִשְׁכָּן־שָׁם֙ הֶֽעָנָ֔ן שָׁ֥ם יַחֲנ֖וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And whenever was taken up the cloud from over the tent, then after that set out [the] sons of Israel; and in [the] place where settled there the cloud, there encamped [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: Each time the cloud was lifted from over the tent, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} would then set out, and at the place where the cloud came to rest, there they made their camp.

L.17: And whenever the cloud was taken up from over the tent, after that the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel would set out; and in the place where the cloud settled, there the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel would camp.

R.17: Whenever the cloud rose up from over the tent, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} packed up and moved on. When the cloud came down and stayed in a place, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} set up their camp there.

decisions.choice: to the mouth of: whenever, at the time that
decisions.reason: The phrase "to the mouth of" can mean "according to" or "whenever". Here it marks each time the cloud lifted. Verse 18 uses a close phrase, "on the mouth of the LORD", for his command.

decisions.choice: was taken up: lifted, rose from the tent
decisions.reason: The verb is passive, "was taken up". The text does not say who lifted it, but the next verse makes clear that the LORD gave the signal.

decisions.choice: settled: the same root as "tabernacle"
decisions.reason: The verb means to settle or dwell, and the word for tabernacle (*mishkan*) means "dwelling" and comes from it. The cloud resting on the tent shows the LORD living among his people (Exodus 25:8; 40:35).

decisions.choice: set out ... camped: broke camp and moved on, then stopped
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 40:36: "set out" is to pull up the tent pegs and move on; "camp" is to stop and pitch the tents.

decisions.choice: packed up and moved on
decisions.reason: Readable says what setting out involved; Literal and Balanced keep "set out".

records.source: עַל־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֗ה יִסְעוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְעַל־פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה יַחֲנ֑וּ כָּל־יְמֵ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁכֹּ֧ן הֶעָנָ֛ן עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן יַחֲנֽוּ׃
records.gloss: On [the] mouth of Yahweh set out [the] sons of Israel, and on [the] mouth of Yahweh they encamped; all [the] days that settled the cloud over the tabernacle they encamped.
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} set out when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded and camped when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded. They stayed in camp for as long as the cloud remained over the tabernacle.

L.18: At the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel would set out, and at the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} they would camp; all the days that the cloud settled over the tabernacle they would stay in camp.

R.18: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} moved on when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told them to, and they camped when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told them to. As long as the cloud stayed over the tabernacle, they stayed where they were.

decisions.choice: on the mouth of Yahweh: at the LORD's command
decisions.reason: The "mouth" of the LORD is what he says, his order (Exodus 17:1). The cloud's movement was the way his order was given.

decisions.choice: the mouth of Yahweh, repeated: Israel's journey under God's direction
decisions.reason: The phrase comes seven times in verses 18-23. The point of the passage is not the cloud itself but that every move and every halt was at the LORD's word.

decisions.choice: when the LORD commanded / when the LORD told them to
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom; Literal keeps "at the mouth of the LORD", as in Exodus 17:1.

records.source: וּבְהַאֲרִ֧יךְ הֶֽעָנָ֛ן עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וְשָׁמְר֧וּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֥רֶת יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א יִסָּֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: And when lengthened the cloud over the tabernacle many days, then kept [the] sons of Israel the charge of Yahweh and not they set out.
pieces: If the cloud stayed on over the tabernacle for many days, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} kept the charge of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and did not move on.

L.19: And when the cloud lingered over the tabernacle many days, the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel kept the charge of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and did not set out.

R.19: Sometimes the cloud stayed over the tabernacle for many days. Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} obeyed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and did not leave.

decisions.choice: lingered: stayed a long time
decisions.reason: The verb means "made long": the cloud stayed on and on.

decisions.choice: kept the charge of Yahweh: did what the LORD required
decisions.reason: The word means a duty given to someone to watch over (3:7-8; Leviticus 8:35). Here the duty is to wait: staying in camp, however long, was itself obedience.

decisions.choice: obeyed
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "kept the charge"; Literal and Balanced keep the phrase, as in Leviticus 8:35.

records.source: וְיֵ֞שׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִהְיֶ֧ה הֶֽעָנָ֛ן יָמִ֥ים מִסְפָּ֖ר עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עַל־פִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ יַחֲנ֔וּ וְעַל־פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה יִסָּֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: And there were [times] when was the cloud days of number over the tabernacle; on [the] mouth of Yahweh they encamped and on [the] mouth of Yahweh they set out.
pieces: At times the cloud remained over the tabernacle for just a few days. They camped when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded and set out when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded.

L.20: And there were [times] when the cloud was a few days over the tabernacle; at the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} they would camp, and at the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} they would set out.

R.20: At other times the cloud was over the tabernacle for only a few days. They camped when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told them to, and they moved on when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told them to.

decisions.choice: days of number: a few days
decisions.reason: Days "of number" are days that can easily be counted, that is, few (Genesis 34:30; Deuteronomy 4:27).

decisions.choice: there is when: sometimes
decisions.reason: The phrase means "there were times when". Verses 20-22 list how long the cloud might stay, from a single night to longer than a month.

decisions.choice: when the LORD commanded
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

records.source: וְיֵ֞שׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִהְיֶ֤ההֶֽעָנָן֙ מֵעֶ֣רֶב עַד־בֹּ֔קֶר וְנַעֲלָ֧ה הֶֽעָנָ֛ן בַּבֹּ֖קֶר וְנָסָ֑עוּ א֚וֹ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלַ֔יְלָה וְנַעֲלָ֥ה הֶעָנָ֖ן וְנָסָֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: And there were [times] when was the cloud from evening until morning, and was taken up the cloud in the morning, and they set out; or by day and night, and was taken up the cloud, and they set out.
pieces: There were times when the cloud remained only from evening to morning; when it was lifted at daybreak, they moved on. Or if it remained a day and a night, they moved on when the cloud was lifted.

L.21: And there were [times] when the cloud was [there] from evening until morning; and when the cloud was taken up in the morning, they would set out. Or [if it stayed] a day and a night, when the cloud was taken up, they would set out.

R.21: Sometimes the cloud stayed only from evening until morning. When it lifted in the morning, they moved on. Or it might stay for a day and a night. When it lifted, they moved on.

decisions.choice: or by day and night: if it stayed a full day and night
alternatives: whether by day or by night, whenever the cloud lifted
decisions.reason: The words can describe how long the cloud stayed, a day and a night, which follows on from "evening until morning" before them and "two days" after them (verse 22). They can also say when the people moved: by day or by night, whenever the cloud lifted. The list of lengths in verses 20-22 favors the first reading.

decisions.choice: if it stayed / if it remained / it might stay
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is brief: "or by day and night". Each level supplies what is understood from the first half of the verse.

records.source: אֽוֹ־יֹמַ֜יִם אוֹ־חֹ֣דֶשׁ אוֹ־יָמִ֗ים בְּהַאֲרִ֨יךְ הֶעָנָ֤ן עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּן֙ לִשְׁכֹּ֣ן עָלָ֔יו יַחֲנ֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְלֹ֣א יִסָּ֑עוּ וּבְהֵעָלֹת֖וֹ יִסָּֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: Or two days, or a month, or days, when lengthened the cloud over the tabernacle to dwell over it, encamped [the] sons of Israel and not they set out; and when it was taken up they set out.
pieces: Two days, a month or longer: however long the cloud lingered over the tabernacle, resting on it, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} stayed in camp and did not move on; but once it was lifted, they moved on.

L.22: Or [whether] two days, or a month, or days, when the cloud lingered over the tabernacle, settling over it, the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel would stay in camp and not set out; but when it was taken up, they would set out.

R.22: The cloud might stay over the tabernacle for two days, or a month, or even longer. As long as it stayed, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} stayed in camp and did not leave. But when it lifted, they moved on.

decisions.choice: days: a longer time, perhaps a year
decisions.reason: The plain word "days" after "two days" and "a month" must mean a longer stretch. In some passages "days" means a full year (Leviticus 25:29; 1 Samuel 27:7), and that may be the sense here. It may also mean simply "a long time".

decisions.choice: to dwell over it: to rest there
decisions.reason: The verb is the one in verse 17, from the same root as "tabernacle": the cloud stayed and rested on the dwelling.

decisions.choice: or longer / or even longer
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the third, open-ended time span means without fixing it at a year; Literal keeps "days".

records.source: עַל־פִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ יַחֲנ֔וּ וְעַל־פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה יִסָּ֑עוּ אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֤רֶת יְהוָה֙ שָׁמָ֔רוּ עַל־פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ
records.gloss: On [the] mouth of Yahweh they encamped, and on [the] mouth of Yahweh they set out; the charge of Yahweh they kept, on [the] mouth of Yahweh by [the] hand of Moses.
pieces: They camped when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded and set out when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded. They kept the charge of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded through Moses.

L.23: At the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} they would camp, and at the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} they would set out; they kept the charge of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, at the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by the hand of Moses.

R.23: They camped when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told them to, and they moved on when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told them to. They obeyed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and did what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded them through Moses.

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" means by means of someone. The LORD's commands came both by the cloud and by the words Moses passed on (4:37, 45; 10:13).

decisions.choice: the close of the passage: obedience at every step
decisions.reason: The verse gathers up the key phrases of verses 18-22 and adds Moses' part. It prepares for the silver trumpets that will signal the moves (10:1-10) and the first departure from Sinai (10:11-13).

decisions.choice: obeyed
decisions.reason: As in verse 19; Literal and Balanced keep "kept the charge".
